finding: Demand is not the same as supply
plain_meaning: Many annual-report stories begin with demand, but the harder question is whether the system can actually supply the need.
example_companies: power, healthcare, housing, AI, materials, energy
proof_boundary: Demand signals do not prove supply, customer cash, or returns.

finding: Companies matter when they control a hard step
plain_meaning: A company becomes important when it sits between a real need and completion.
money_path: customer burden -> company system -> problem solved -> payment/cash
example_companies: utilities, distributors, healthcare platforms, retailers, payment networks, capital platforms
proof_boundary: A hard step can still be competed away or fail to convert into durable cash.

finding: Power is becoming a gatekeeper for growth
plain_meaning: Electricity must be generated, delivered, approved, financed, billed, and recovered before growth can happen.
money_path: load -> power/grid investment -> regulated or contracted payment -> cash
example_companies: NextEra/FPL, Duke, AEP, Constellation, Vistra, NRG, MasTec, Sterling
proof_boundary: Load forecasts and capital plans are not customer receipts or project returns.

plain_meaning: Large asset managers and insurer-linked platforms route savings and liabilities into assets, borrowers, credit, real estate, and infrastructure.
money_path: saver/policyholder capital -> platform wrapper -> asset/borrower/project -> fees, interest, spread, repayment, sale proceeds
example_companies: BlackRock, Blackstone, Apollo/Athene, KKR/Global Atlantic, Brookfield, Ares, Carlyle
proof_boundary: AUM and inflows are not proof of borrower receipt, legal-entity cash, collateral, waterfall, or final return.

plain_meaning: Healthcare demand is obvious; the scarce part is organized access under reimbursement, labor, pharmacy, and trust pressure.
money_path: patient need -> payer/PBM/provider/care-site -> authorized care/drug/service -> reimbursement/premium/service revenue -> cash
example_companies: UnitedHealth, Cigna, DaVita, Addus, Option Care, HCA, McKesson, Abbott, Stryker
proof_boundary: Revenue and patient volume do not prove care quality, fairness, reimbursement durability, or service-line cash.

finding: The physical world keeps demanding money
plain_meaning: Homes, buildings, water systems, roads, plants, and stores wear out and need recurring upkeep.
money_path: owner/contractor/municipality need -> retailer/distributor/manufacturer/service -> material or repair input -> project/upkeep -> cash
example_companies: Home Depot, Lowe’s, Core & Main, Builders FirstSource, Sherwin-Williams, Ferguson, Vulcan, Steel Dynamics
proof_boundary: Housing exposure is not one thing; each channel has different margin, inventory, receivable, and cycle risk.

plain_meaning: Industrial customers pay for equipment, parts, and service because stopping work is expensive.
money_path: operating need -> rental/parts/service/distribution supplier -> available equipment/inventory/support -> avoided downtime -> revenue/cash
example_companies: United Rentals, Fastenal, WESCO, Grainger, Applied Industrial, MSC, Watsco, MasTec, Sterling
proof_boundary: Branch count, fleet size, and backlog do not prove collection, ROIC, collateral value, or project margin.

plain_meaning: More online activity creates more need for security, identity, policy, traffic routing, governance, and fraud control.
money_path: digital activity -> control need -> security/routing/platform/workflow provider -> subscription/usage/contract/take-rate -> revenue/cash
example_companies: Cloudflare, Akamai, Zscaler, Fortinet, Roblox, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Broadcom, Cisco, ServiceNow
proof_boundary: ARR, RPO, users, AI demand, and traffic do not prove free-cash-flow durability or customer ROI.

finding: The consumer is not one simple story
plain_meaning: Households spend through tradeoffs: price, convenience, habit, identity, relief, quality, and regret reduction.
money_path: household income/stress -> shopping/service/brand/experience choice -> retailer/restaurant/platform/brand -> traffic/margin/fees/cash
example_companies: Costco, Walmart, Target, Dollar General, Burlington, Marriott, Booking, McDonald’s, Starbucks, P&G, Coca-Cola
proof_boundary: Sales do not prove consumer health; price can hide volume weakness and traffic can hide margin pressure.

finding: Materials and energy are the denominators
plain_meaning: Technology, housing, infrastructure, food, data centers, and industry still need physical inputs and routes.
money_path: end demand -> mine/mill/quarry/plant/pipeline/exporter/refiner -> input or energy movement -> price/volume/fee/spread/cash
example_companies: Freeport, Nucor, Steel Dynamics, Vulcan, CF Industries, Exxon, Energy Transfer, ONEOK, Plains, Cheniere
proof_boundary: Commodity strength can reverse; output and tariffs do not prove asset-level returns.

plain_meaning: Digital and physical systems still require towers, warehouses, data centers, medical sites, retail nodes, hotels, and tenant cash.
money_path: tenant/user demand -> scarce site or property asset -> lease/rent/occupancy/renewal/service payment -> property cash flow
example_companies: American Tower, Prologis, Equinix, Welltower, Realty Income, Marriott, MGM
proof_boundary: Real estate value depends on tenant health, debt cost, occupancy, leases, cap rates, and refinancing.

finding: Ordinary finance shows stress moving through daily life
plain_meaning: Deposits, cards, loans, premiums, claims, payment fees, and losses turn daily pressure into measurable financial flows.
money_path: transaction -> bank/card issuer/insurer/lender/payment network -> deposit/loan/premium/fee/claim/provision -> earnings/capital/cash
example_companies: JPMorgan, American Express, Capital One, Progressive, Visa, Synchrony
proof_boundary: Spending does not prove repayment; premium growth does not prove underwriting; volume does not prove merchant health.
